summary: When the project has an approved Process Policy, each backlog review round records its path, revision and source hash, the pin a Delivery takes at scope approval, as the policy in force when the round is written: `backlog_compile.py init`, `stub-epic` and `begin-revision` write their rounds with it, and `check` pins a draft round the Product Owner writes the first time it sees it, reporting it in `pinned_reviews`, never an approved round. `process_policy.py init` and `begin-revision`, the only steps that change the policy in force, first record the state they replace in every draft round that records no policy yet and list those rounds in `pinned_reviews`: `init` records revision 0, which names no policy, and `begin-revision` the approved revision, so no round written before a policy change takes the next policy's pin. `backlog_compile.py approve` records its own pin in `backlog.md` and refuses, before any write, a review it approves that ran with another value, parameters included, of a switch the backlog-planning flow owns than the approval's policy sets, reading the round's values from the current policy or the Git history of its path, or whose pinned revision it cannot read back, naming the remedy: rerun the review in a new round under the current policy, or approve a policy revision that sets those values back. A revision that changes only other switches, such as one set for the next Delivery, leaves the reviews valid, and a round from before the first policy agrees with a policy that keeps every backlog switch at its default. Each round keeps its own pin, so a backlog revision and its reviews outside any Delivery name the process switch values they ran under. The pin follows `approved_at_utc` once approved and sits inside the notes' source and package hashes. After approval it is a record and is never compared: a later policy revision leaves the approved backlog current, a round approved earlier keeps its own pin, and `backlog_compile.py begin-revision` drops the pin from the new draft root until its own approval. A round written while the policy is a draft records nothing and is pinned by the first check after the policy's approval. A draft or invalid policy refuses a new approval before any write; re-approving an unchanged approved backlog is unaffected. Without a policy nothing is recorded, and a new golden all-default approval run proves every backlog file the approval writes byte-identical to the previous release apart from #306's legacy story fix. The `story_size_budget` instructions now leave the policy revision to that record and keep only the limits in an epic review's Slicing evidence.
